test_policy.notes: "Furman University is a SAT/ACT test optional institution." Scores that are submitted are superscored; applicants who do not want scores considered say so on the Common Application (international applicants must still prove English proficiency). The same policy is stated for first-year and international applicants.

requirements.notes: Common Application or Coalition/Scoir Application. "Furman does not have an application fee." Required first-year steps listed for 2026-2027: the application, an official high school transcript and the counselor's School Report; the steps list no recommendation letters and does not say whether there is a writing supplement, so those fields are left blank. International applicants submit the transcript and school report in English (a NACES course-by-course evaluation may be requested), an English proficiency test or exemption, the Furman Financial Information Form (on the status page) and the CSS Profile: "All international applicants must fill out the Furman Financial Information Form ... in addition to completing the CSS Profile. Furman is unable to provide CSS Profile waivers." Interview: Furman partners with Vericant and Initial View, which "do not evaluate candidates but, instead, post the interviews online for our admissions team to review"; "Although the interview is not mandatory, we highly recommend you participate." The first-year page headed 'Required steps to apply (2026-2027)' gives these dates, so they are read as the 2026-27 cycle (fall 2027 entry). A second, older Furman page (international-admissions/apply) still shows other dates and a COVID-era fee waiver; it was not used.

deadlines.label: Early Decision I
deadlines.notes: Binding. Same dates on the first-year and international pages. Enrollment deadline January 5. As of the access date (2026-11-03) this deadline has just passed.

deadlines.label: Early Action
deadlines.notes: Non-binding. Enrollment deadline May 1. As of the access date (2026-11-03) this deadline has just passed.

deadlines.label: Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: Enrollment deadline May 1. The international page lists no earlier date than the first-year page.

deadlines.label: #YouAreWelcomeHere Scholarship application (international students)
deadlines.notes: Two awards covering at least 50% of tuition, renewable; application on the Furman status page by February 1, recipients notified by March 15, deposit by May 1. The page prints no year.

english_policy.waiver_notes: "Furman requires proof of English proficiency from all non-native English-speaking international students." Exempt at admission: citizens of the listed countries (Australia, Canada except Quebec, Ireland, New Zealand, Nigeria, Singapore, South Africa, United Kingdom, Ghana, Kenya and others on the page). Also accepted: completion of the IB Diploma with Higher Level English grade 5 or better; a C (2.0) or higher in two U.S. college English composition courses; SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing 550 or higher; four full years of secondary school in the U.S. (with at least 3 full years of English); or a letter from the school confirming English is the primary language of instruction. Self-reported scores are accepted for admission review, but enrolling students must send official scores.

english.notes: 'Minimum scores required' list: TOEFL (0-120) 100. TOEFL code 5222.
Duolingo English Test 120; Furman is unable to provide fee waivers.

aid.notes: Furman's financial-aid page says: "International students are eligible for all institutional merit-based scholarships but are not eligible for need-based grants." Merit awards need no separate application ("Your application for admission automatically serves as your application for merit-based scholarships"); the FAQ says academic scholarships go up to full tuition per year, and the James B. Duke Scholarship covers tuition, room, board and fees. Two #YouAreWelcomeHere awards (at least 50% of tuition) are for international students. Even so, every international applicant must file the CSS Profile and the Furman Financial Information Form. Conflicts to be aware of: the Common Data Set ticks need-based institutional aid for nonresidents, and Furman's tuition page says "We meet 100% of demonstrated financial need for eligible students" (it does not say whether international students are eligible); the CDS shows first-year students' average need met at 83.68% (all aided students). merit_only follows the college's statement about international students.

tier_notes.computer_science: Judgment call: Computer Science, Data Science and Data and Decision Analytics majors at a college of about 2,300 undergraduates; placed below the general tier.
tier_notes.business: Judgment call: Business Administration, Accounting and Finance majors at a small liberal-arts university; regional rather than top-40 national standing.
tier_notes.biology_life_sci: Judgment call: biology, health sciences and public health majors at a small college; placed below the general tier.
tier_notes.pre_med: Judgment call: a Pre-Health program and Health Sciences major at a small college; placed below the general tier.
tier_notes.economics: Judgment call: Economics, Mathematics-Economics and Finance-Economics majors at a small college; placed below the general tier.
tier_notes.math_physics: Judgment call: small mathematics and physics departments in a college of about 2,300 undergraduates.
tier_notes.humanities: Judgment call: liberal-arts humanities departments at a small college; placed below the general tier.
tier_notes.arts_design: Judgment call: music, art and theatre are offered (music has an audition-based scholarship process); no design school.
tier_notes.engineering: No engineering major of its own: the programs page lists only a 'Dual-Degree Engineering Program' attached to the Physics and Applied Physics majors.
